name: TX-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district fundamentals strongly favor Republicans
Incumbent Keith Self holds cash and outside-spending advantages
Prediction markets price Self's win odds near 94%
Challenger Evan Hunt's fundraising trails with low cash on hand
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, Self's incumbency with a cash and outside-spending edge, and market pricing near 94% Republican all point the same direction, and no polls or ratings suggest a competitive race. Hunt's challenger fundraising is credible but his low cash on hand limits his ability to close a double-digit structural gap.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending behind Hunt or emerging polling showing a single-digit margin would justify moving this race toward the competitive column.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Keith Self returns after renomination with the advantages that typically follow: name recognition, a fundraising edge, and outside support. Democrat Evan Hunt has raised a credible sum for a challenger in this territory, but he enters the final stretch with far less cash on hand, limiting his ability to introduce himself to voters.

No public polls or expert ratings track this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point firmly to Self. Prediction markets give Hunt roughly a one-in-twenty chance. A strong national Democratic environment could tighten the contest, but the district's baseline margin has historically absorbed such swings. Self remains the clear favorite to hold the seat.
